body:
Pipelines should be compiled on a background thread when using background loading as long as the material is assigned to the surface at load time. 

Is there any chance you are assigning the material after loading, or doing something that would have the same effect like assigning the material to a material override slot instead of assigning it to the surface directly?

> Pipelines should be compiled on a background thread when using background loading as long as the material is assigned to the surface at load time.
> 
> Is there any chance you are assigning the material after loading, or doing something that would have the same effect like assigning the material to a material override slot instead of assigning it to the surface directly?

Sorry for the slow response. Agreed they should be, but there are some gaps:

One concrete example is `RenderForwardClustered::_mesh_compile_pipelines_for_surface` compiles a pipeline for `PIPELINE_VERSION_DEPTH_PASS_WITH_NORMAL_AND_ROUGHNESS` but not `PIPELINE_VERSION_DEPTH_PASS_WITH_NORMAL_AND_ROUGHNESS_MULTIVIEW`.

The other case is with XR depth submission (which is an optional feature). When MSAA is not used, Godot renders directly into this texture which does not have a format that `_mesh_compile_pipelines_for_surface` expected.

The problem can get magnified because any pipelines not precompiled before rendering (which would happen in worker threads) will cause a stall at render time, compiling and waiting on each missing pipeline case one-by-one.
